rationale: Bead 2 can use the general lock callback and can tighten the sanctioned-call fence without redesign, but bead 1 is not safe or verified enough to integrate. SanctionedDerivedSync discards the child-read error and derives plan from the resulting nil slice, so bead 2's release wiring can turn failed discovery into a sanctioned backward write. The required go test ./... -short gate is red in the reviewed linked worktree because repair tests resolve the lock to the shared main checkout, where the lock cannot be opened in this review sandbox; an untracked main-checkout .mindspec/phase.lock is present and is not ignored by main's pre-merge .gitignore. AC-5(v)'s claimed barrier test and AC-5(vii)'s migration-contention test use sleeps rather than an acquisition-attempt barrier, so they can pass without proving the loser contended. The AC-5(vi) inventory test is also not total: it detects string-keyed composite literals, not MergeMetadata write dataflow, and misses writers assembled through index assignment or helpers.
concrete_changes_required: Make SanctionedDerivedSync propagate GetChildren/derivation-read failures and add behavioral tests proving no metadata write occurs on read failure, plus a success test over the real lock/merge seam before bead 2 wires release.

Make the repair tests hermetic in linked worktrees by injecting or otherwise fixture-scoping the lock root while preserving production's shared repo lock, and ensure the required full short suite passes from the bead worktree without creating blockable dirt in the main checkout.

Replace the sleep-based phaselock and migration-contention scheduling with deterministic attempt/blocked/release barriers; assert the second contender has attempted acquisition before releasing the first, cannot enter before release, does enter afterward, and returns no error.

Strengthen the AC-5(vi) inventory test to enumerate actual MergeMetadata-family phase writes independent of map-construction syntax, including index-assignment/helper-built update maps, and prove red-on-new-unlocked-writer behavior.
Remove the untracked shared-main .mindspec/phase.lock once no process holds it; the reviewed bead worktree itself is currently clean.

findings.title: SanctionedDerivedSync fabricates plan when child discovery fails
findings.evidence: internal/phase/sanctioned_sync.go calls children, _ := c.GetChildren(epicID), then DerivePhaseFromChildren(children). A read error therefore becomes nil children and plan, which is written under the sanctioned backward bypass. There are no behavioral tests for SanctionedDerivedSync, only its caller-enumeration fence.
findings.next_bead_impact: Bead 2 replaces release's current pre-derivation guard with this surface; a bd read failure after release mutation could then write plan rather than suppressing the sync.

findings.title: Required short suite is red and linked-worktree lock dirt is not covered
findings.evidence: go build ./... completed, but go test ./... -short failed in cmd/mindspec: TestRepairPhase_BackwardMoveRefused, TestRepairPhase_ForceBackwardWritesAndRecordsReason, TestRepairPhase_WritesDerivedViaMergeSeam, and TestRepairPhase_AlreadyConsistentStillMergeWrites all tried /Users/Max/replit/mindspec/.mindspec/phase.lock and received operation not permitted. git -C /Users/Max/replit/mindspec status --porcelain -- .mindspec/phase.lock reports an untracked lock file, while the ignore entry exists only in the bead branch. The no-dirt test uses a standalone temp repo and does not exercise linked-worktree root resolution. The bead worktree's own git status is clean.

findings.title: AC-5(v) barrier test is timing-based and can pass vacuously
findings.evidence: TestWithPhaseWriteLock_ExclusiveAcrossGoroutines releases the first holder after a 50ms sleep. It has no signal that the second goroutine attempted acquisition before release, does not assert that second entry is impossible while the holder remains blocked, ignores both lock-call errors, and only checks maxInside > 1. A schedule where contender two starts after release passes.

findings.title: AC-5(vii) migration-contention test does not prove real contention
findings.evidence: TestEnsureMigrated_NeverOverwritesFresherLockedWrite starts EnsureMigrated, sleeps 50ms, and releases the holder without an observable acquisition-attempt barrier. The test can pass if EnsureMigrated is not scheduled until after release; it then sees plan and no-ops without having contended. Twenty race-enabled repetitions passed, but that validates race freedom, not the intended interleaving.

findings.title: AC-5(vi) writer inventory is syntax-shaped rather than total
findings.evidence: writer_inventory_test.go marks string-keyed mindspec_phase entries in composite literals as guarded when lexically nested in WithPhaseWriteLock. A new unlocked MergeMetadata writer using updates := map[string]interface{}{} followed by updates["mindspec_phase"] = value, or a helper-built map, is invisible. It also does not anchor detection to MergeMetadata-family calls as AC-5(vi) requires.

findings.title: Deviation A assessment
findings.assessment: The root/epicID/mergeMetadata/callback signature is an acceptable and more useful divergence from the plan shorthand. It preserves per-caller write seams, supports next's new writer, and can atomically write phase plus the semantics-v2 marker. The signature is not the problem; the accompanying inventory test overclaims totality and must be strengthened.

findings.title: Deviation B assessment
findings.assessment: Acceptable mechanical change. All three production callers pass root, the repository builds, and the cache-aware shape remains usable by EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2. Test-root handling is deficient, but adding root to the API is correct for locating the shared lock.

findings.title: Deviation C assessment
findings.assessment: Acceptable and honestly disclosed. The added arg2 registry entry mirrors the existing repairPhaseRunE arg1 residual, identifies the same unvalidated specID/derived epicID provenance, notes idrender rendering without pretending it proves validation, and is paired with the lint manifest entry.

findings.title: Deviation D assessment
findings.assessment: Acceptable. The AST anchors now match WithPhaseWriteLock with implPhaseMetadataFn as the third argument and inspect the callback's returned map; they retain the prior reconcile-before-close and done-write-after-close ordering assertions without weakening their phase/done disambiguation.

findings.title: Bead-2 fence and lock integration assessment
findings.assessment: The sanctioned-call walker already returns file and enclosing function, so bead 2 can tighten it from subset-of-allowlist to exactly one cmd/mindspec/release.go syncPhase call with a small assertion change. WithPhaseWriteLock's map-return callback is adequate for next's first-lifecycle-claim advance and EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2's combined marker/phase update. Targeted go test -race ./internal/phase/... passed, including 20 repeated runs of the two named contention tests, but the tests' synchronization gaps remain.
